LanguageData.FDR_Empty: Empty. Haul fish here to begin drying.
LanguageData.FDR_BatchSpoiling: The catch on {0} has started to spoil in the heat.
LanguageData.FDR_BatchSpoiled: The catch on {0} has spoiled in the heat.
LanguageData.FDR_SectionThroughputDesc: How much fish a rack turns into how much food, and how long it takes. Both are safe to change with a colony loaded.
LanguageData.FDR_SectionEnvironmentDesc: How much the world around a rack matters. Turn these down if you want a simple building, or leave them alone for the full simulation.
LanguageData.FDR_SetDryingTimeDesc: How long a batch hangs before it is done. Lower is faster. Progress is stored as a percentage, so changing this mid-save only affects the time still ahead of you - a rack at 60% stays at 60%.
LanguageData.FDR_ExDryingTime: Right now: a full rack takes about {0} days in ideal conditions.
LanguageData.FDR_SetYieldDesc: How much dried fish comes out the other end. At 100% the conversion matches jerky exactly, so a rack of fish is worth the same as a rack of meat. Raise it if fish are scarce on your map, lower it if your colony is drowning in them.
LanguageData.FDR_ExYield: Right now: a full rack ({0} nutrition of fish) yields about {1} dried fish.
LanguageData.FDR_SetDeteriorationDesc: How fast dried fish degrades when left uncovered. It never rots and never needs refrigeration, but a stack sitting out in the weather should not last forever. Only applies outdoors - anything under a roof degrades more slowly, and anything indoors never degrades at all. Rain multiplies the effect, so wet climates are harsher. For scale: packaged survival meals are 0.25 and rice is 6. Set to 0 to make dried fish indestructible like jerky.
LanguageData.FDR_ExDeterioration: Right now: an exposed stack would take roughly {0} days to degrade completely, before weather and roofing are taken into account. Indoors, never.
LanguageData.FDR_ExDeteriorationNever: Right now: dried fish never deteriorates, anywhere.
LanguageData.FDR_SetTemperatureDesc: How much the weather's temperature changes drying speed. Fish dry best just above freezing - cold enough that they don't rot, warm enough that they aren't frozen solid. At 0% a rack works identically in a desert and a glacier. At 100% cold biomes are genuinely better places to dry fish.
LanguageData.FDR_ExTemperature: Right now: a warm day (20C / 68F) dries at {0} speed, deep cold (-20C / -4F) at {1}.
LanguageData.FDR_SetCrowdingDesc: How badly racks packed into a sealed room slow each other down. The moisture coming off the fish has to go somewhere, and in a closed room it just sits there. Only ever affects racks indoors - outdoor racks are never crowded. At 0% you can line a walk-in freezer with racks and they all run at full speed.
LanguageData.FDR_ExCrowding: Right now: 4 racks in a roomy 11x11 hall run at {0} speed; 4 crammed into a 30-tile freezer, {1}.
LanguageData.FDR_SetWindDesc: Wind is what actually dries fish on a rack. With this on, outdoor racks speed up in a gale and stall in still air, a roof overhead cuts some of the wind, and indoor racks get none of it at all - which is what makes indoor drying slow but perfectly predictable. Wind is map-wide and set by the weather, so it is luck rather than a decision. Turn this off if you would rather outdoor drying were steady.
LanguageData.FDR_SetRainDesc: An uncovered rack stops completely while it rains. A bare roof on posts prevents this without walling the rack in, which is what a real drying shed is for. Turning this off removes the reason to build that roof, since the roof still costs you a little wind.
LanguageData.FDR_SetSpoilageDesc: What happens to a batch left hanging above 32C / 90F. Spoilage builds up over roughly two days at that temperature and far faster in real heat; you get a warning as it starts. Colonists will not carry fish to a rack that is already too hot.
LanguageData.FDR_SpoilOffDesc: Heat never ruins a batch. Racks work anywhere, at any temperature. Also clears any spoilage already accumulated.
LanguageData.FDR_SpoilForgivingDesc: Spoilage slowly reverses once the rack cools down, so a passing heatwave is survivable if you act.
LanguageData.FDR_SpoilPermanentDesc: Spoilage never reverses. Cooling a rack stops the damage getting worse but does not undo it - fish that has begun to turn has begun to turn.
